cards.text: Proverbs is the wisdom of Solomon, son of David, king of Israel (Prov 1:1). Here he's talking to someone he calls my son, and he opens with a big if: if you've put up security for your neighbor, if you've shaken hands on a pledge with a stranger. Friend, that's the 'what could possibly go wrong' handshake.

cards.question: Solomon keeps going with the ifs. If a pledge like that has trapped the son, what did the trapping?

answers.text: The words of his own mouth
A thief hiding by the road
A debt his father left him

cards.text: Solomon says the son has fallen into his neighbor's hands. Worst place to fall, friend, and I've fallen face-first into the chocolate chips MANY times.

cards.question: To get free, Solomon tells the son to go to his neighbor, ___ himself, and press his plea.
True or false: Solomon tells the son this can wait until he's had a good night's sleep.

cards.text: No sleep for the eyes, no slumber for the eyelids. Friend, this is not a snooze-button problem, this is a one-sock-on, keys-in-your-teeth, out-the-door problem.

cards.question: Solomon tells the son to free himself like a gazelle from the hand of the hunter, like a bird from the snare of the fowler. What's he telling the son to do?

answers.text: Get loose quickly while he still can
Hide quietly until the trouble passes
Turn and fight whoever set the trap

cards.text: Then Solomon calls out the slacker, and he hands the slacker a teacher straight from the animal world.

cards.question: Which creature does Solomon tell the slacker to learn from?

cards.text: Solomon says to observe its ways and become wise. A grown person, sent to take notes from a BUG, and friend, I'd be sitting right there in the front row with my mustache raised.

cards.question: True or false: The ant has a commander standing over it, making sure it gets its work done.
The ant prepares its provisions in summer and gathers its food at harvest. What makes that so wise?

answers.text: It gets ready before it needs to
It saves food for other creatures
It rests once the work is done

cards.text: Then Solomon asks the slacker how long he'll lie there and when he'll get up from his sleep. Friend, I lay in a drawer for YEARS and didn't even have a choice, so get UP.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says the slacker's trouble starts with one big, long nap.

cards.text: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest. Nobody ever says, "I'm about to ruin my life," friend, they just say, "Five more minutes."

cards.question: All that little rest adds up. Solomon says poverty will come upon the slacker like a robber, so just like a robber, it shows up ___.

cards.text: Poverty like a robber, need like a bandit. Nobody puts the robber on their calendar, friend.
New picture now. Solomon describes a worthless person, a wicked man who walks around with a perverse mouth.

cards.question: This wicked man doesn't only talk with his mouth. What else does he talk with?

answers.text: His eyes and feet and fingers
Songs and riddles at the gate

cards.text: Winking his eyes, speaking with his feet, pointing with his fingers. This man is a whole group chat, and he's typing with his ENTIRE body.

cards.question: With deceit in his heart, the wicked man devises evil and keeps sowing ___.

cards.text: Then Solomon says therefore. Everything this man has been planting is about to come up.

cards.question: What does Solomon say will come upon the wicked man?

answers.text: A slow and quiet decline over time

cards.text: In an instant, shattered beyond recovery, like a cookie hitting a tile floor. There is no five-second rule for THAT, friend.
Then Solomon gives a list: six things the LORD hates, seven that are detestable to Him. Lean in, friend, because number one is haughty eyes.

cards.question: True or false: A lying tongue is on the list of things the LORD hates.
The LORD's list goes on to hands that shed innocent blood. Haughty eyes, a lying tongue, hands. What do the first three things on the list have in common?

answers.text: Each one is a part of the body
Each one is a sin of the priests
Each one is a sin against parents

cards.question: The LORD also hates a ___ that devises wicked schemes, and ___ that run swiftly to evil.

cards.text: Number six on the list: a false witness who gives false testimony. One more to go.

cards.question: What's number seven, the last thing on the LORD's list?

answers.text: One who stirs up discord among brothers
One who turns away from the poor
One who breaks a promise to a friend

cards.text: Discord again: the wicked man was busy sowing it, and now it closes out the LORD's whole list. So friend, if your hobby is starting drama, this is NOT the shout-out you were hoping for.

findings.problem: The punchline 'so get UP' turns Solomon's rebuke of the slacker onto the baker. It tells the baker directly to stop lying around, which reads as calling the baker a slacker.

The card before it (card 13) asks 'how long will you lie there,' which points the baker toward one long stretch of sleep. That makes 'True' look right. Nothing before this card lets the baker work out that the trouble comes from a little sleep at a time (6:10), so getting it right is luck.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: 'wheat' is a literal crop, while 'discord' and 'kindness' are moral qualities, so the answers are not the same kind of thing.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The question itself says 'With deceit in his heart, the wicked man devises evil,' which rules out 'kindness.' With 'wheat' also out of place, only one answer is left that makes sense.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
